title: Expose verified task progress as a disabled-by-default read-only developer preview
request: Complete the Task Plan panel in the existing app, keep execution rollout blocked, test planning within the authorized dollar cap and permanently collect all test records.
plan: Inspect existing settings, project access, task checkpoints and browser conventions.
Write failing read-only presenter and API tests, then project allowlisted metadata without verification writers.
Add the existing-design task tree, owner preview setting, responsive states and rollback.
Exercise relevant file, PostgreSQL and browser paths, independently review, preserve all results and record limits.

decisions.decision: Use existing owner-only audited team settings with a false default.
decisions.why: The failed execution promotion gate permits a preview but cannot justify a new execution switch.

decisions.decision: Read the existing saver with storage-enforced read-only connections and no setup.
decisions.why: A progress GET must neither create storage nor write verification, reconciliation or task effects.

decisions.decision: Show completion only with matching recorded verification and current owner evidence.
decisions.why: An attempt status or model claim does not establish scientific acceptance; missing upstream proof must block descendants.

decisions.decision: Keep full model exchanges in the opted-out diagnostic archive and only allowlisted metadata in the app.
decisions.why: The owner requires thinking capture while private reasoning and data must not appear in product traces or training.

decisions.decision: Keep proposed hierarchy execution unmeasured while testing model task plans on the deterministic hierarchy.
decisions.why: The current dispatcher refuses candidate model graphs; narrower successful execution cannot authorize full rollout.

decisions.decision: Use an independent permanent USD reservation ceiling with provider-verified prices.
decisions.why: The gateway currency field names and stale application prices cannot alone enforce the owner dollar cap.

change: Add a read-only task presenter, project GET route, owner preview setting and existing-design Task Plan tree with verified progress, evidence, approval, revision history and execution budget. Rebuild generated assets and preserve targeted validation records.

findings.defect: Existing checkpoint and verification helpers can mutate storage during a progress read.
findings.scenario: A newly opened project could trigger saver setup, or a progress refresh could append a proof or reconcile an effect.
findings.cause: Normal runtime constructors and verification routines are designed for execution turns, not a read-only view.
findings.fix: Open only existing storage in enforced read-only mode, bypass saver setup and compare saved proofs with current owner fingerprints without verification or reconciliation.
findings.test: File and PostgreSQL presenter tests prohibit setup, tool calls and proof writes; default-off access creates no database.

findings.defect: A downstream task stayed completed after its upstream verification proof disappeared.
findings.scenario: A fully completed chain lost the saved data verification; later tasks still displayed completed even though their prerequisite was unverified.
findings.cause: The initial projection propagated stale evidence but did not propagate missing-proof blocked states.
findings.fix: Propagate blocked and stale prerequisites through dependent nodes and replace misleading current verification labels.
findings.test: The lost-upstream-proof regression failed before the fix and passed afterward for file and PostgreSQL stores.

findings.defect: A replacement-plan summary counted the retried task as preserved work.
findings.scenario: A completed replacement attempt was listed among tasks preserved across its own replacement.
findings.cause: The preservation list filtered completed actions without excluding the replaced task.
findings.fix: Exclude the retried task and show revision changes as field names without raw plan contents.
findings.test: The replacement-diff regression failed before the fix and passed afterward in both stores.

findings.defect: Historical invalidation hid a newer valid preserved attempt and revision comparisons skipped intermediate graphs.
findings.scenario: After an old data attempt was invalidated and a new data attempt completed, a later confirmation preserved the new attempt but the view showed no preserved work and compared the first graph directly with the latest.
findings.cause: The initial history compared every graph to the current graph and globally excluded task identifiers from any invalidated historical attempt.
findings.fix: Compare adjacent graph versions and derive currently valid preservation from the active attempt that predates the transition.
findings.test: The new multi-revision regression failed before the fix; all presenter tests including its inherited PostgreSQL case pass afterward.

findings.defect: Task status used an evidence-control helper and lost its visible status label.
findings.scenario: The real page showed currency-style evidence chips instead of completed and blocked task labels.
findings.cause: The shared chip helper accepts evidence identifiers, not status labels.
findings.fix: Use the existing plain status tag and assert actual labels and absence of evidence controls on task summaries.
findings.test: The browser label assertion failed before the fix; final desktop and mobile checks pass in both display modes.

findings.defect: A possible cross-workspace audit destination needed verification.
findings.scenario: A service context from another workspace was active when changing the selected workspace preview setting.
findings.cause: The route reused a context audit sink whose destination behavior was not obvious from the call site.
findings.fix: No code change: the existing audit writer resolves the selected workspace correctly; retain the regression.
findings.test: The focused audit-scope regression passed before any change and remains in the API group.

findings.defect: The first browser check could not launch the pinned Chromium executable.
findings.scenario: The repository Playwright version requested a browser revision that was absent from the local cache.
findings.cause: Available browser binaries did not match the installed Playwright runtime.
findings.fix: Install the matching Chromium with the existing environment and keep the failed launch plus successful rerun.
findings.test: The final targeted browser checks pass after the recorded installation.

findings.defect: The browser keeper declined the complete temporary workspace copy.
findings.scenario: The real browser checks passed but available disk was below the existing keeper threshold.
findings.cause: The full workspace copy was refused by its resource guard.
findings.fix: Keep the guard; explicitly save screenshots and invented project, task checkpoint and owner JSON fixtures before teardown, and archive those records.
findings.test: Each final browser check keeps its actual screenshot and fixture; full workspace retention remains a documented limit.
findings.open: Complete temporary workspace copies were not retained.

findings.defect: The initial targeted planning runner could not create its macOS socket.
findings.scenario: The parallel runner startup failed before testing because the temporary path exceeded the local socket length limit.
findings.cause: The inherited temporary directory path left insufficient room for the runner socket name.
findings.fix: Use a short temporary root for this recorded evaluation and preserve the first failure.
findings.test: The subsequent planning group run passed every selected test without skips.

measurements.name: Relevant planning regression groups
measurements.gate: Every selected planning test must pass with zero skips; retain both file and PostgreSQL coverage.
measurements.result: 315 tests in ten planning files passed, zero failures and zero skips; the earlier socket startup failure is retained.
limits: The groups cover task planning and affected owners; no full repository gate ran.

measurements.name: Preview application tests
measurements.gate: All selected presenter, API, team settings, web client and web generation checks must pass without skips.
measurements.result: 57 distinct application tests passed: 33 task presenter/API tests and 24 existing team/web tests, zero skips.
limits: Tests cover actual file and PostgreSQL stores; execution promotion is a separate gate.

measurements.name: Final real browser checks
measurements.gate: The task panel must pass at 1280 and 375 pixels in Developer and Data science modes, with read-only refresh and visible error recovery.
measurements.result: All four final browser checks passed, with actual screenshots and explicit invented fixtures. The whole temporary workspace copy was skipped below the existing 2 GB threshold.
limits: Screenshots and fixture JSON were retained; the whole temporary browser workspace was not copied.

measurements.name: Owner-capped live planning diagnostic
measurements.gate: Never exceed USD 2 reserved exposure; no planning effects, no unauthorized or repeated handlers, and at most one holdout read in each completed run.
measurements.result: 27 model requests on four fresh invented scenarios; token-priced USD 0.025211 and permanently reserved USD 0.08684772. All 27 full replies and returned reasoning records were retained. Three workflows completed with one holdout read each; the changed-contract scenario stopped with zero holdout reads. Zero unauthorized, repeated or leaking handlers and zero offered tool schemas during planning.
measurements.next: Measure proposed-hierarchy execution only after a reviewed dispatcher integration and a newly frozen independent evaluation.
limits: These are provider-catalog token prices, not an invoice.
Task plans ran on the deterministic graph; complete model-hierarchy execution remains unavailable.
The frozen promotion failure is unchanged; the small diagnostic does not establish general benefit.

measurements.name: Execution release boundary
measurements.gate: Only a passed frozen promotion gate can authorize execution rollout.
measurements.result: The historical 45/48 correctness is below the required 95%; the complete model-hierarchy execution arm remains unmeasured. Execution stays disabled and only the read-only preview is delivered.
limits: The preview adds visibility and does not improve the frozen comparison.

measurements.name: Final independent review
measurements.gate: Resolve all confirmed correctness findings and obtain independent review acceptance.
measurements.result: PASS with no remaining correctness finding; the independently recorded revision regression passed one test.
limits: The review supports this preview diff; execution promotion remains blocked.

measurements.name: Development corpus validation
measurements.gate: Generate the corpus with zero refused examples and pass all four validation and freshness tests.
measurements.result: The generated corpus has zero refused examples and all four validation and freshness checks pass.

outcome: The read-only Task Plan developer preview is complete with independent review, 57 distinct relevant application tests, four final browser checks and four completion-corpus checks. Execution stays blocked. The separate live diagnostic remained within the owner cap; all logs, failures, screenshots and invented fixtures are collected through the immutable local archive.
lessons: A read-only endpoint must avoid saver setup and proof-writing verification helpers.
Loss of upstream proof must invalidate dependent completion claims in the view.
Check visible labels in the actual browser; a shared helper name can conceal different semantics.
Keep failed checks and resource retention limits beside successful reruns.
Separate task-plan execution evidence from proposed hierarchy execution evidence.
Use independent permanent reservations when a budget currency differs from gateway field names.
risks: A progress view could otherwise mutate checkpoints or imply unsupported completion.
Raw plans or exception text could expose private information.
A preview switch could be confused with execution authorization.
Small invented live cases cannot justify promotion.
